wireCalibration.measuredBasis: Settle, no scroll. Cold load, first-party encoded bytes (Resource Timing encodedBodySize), brotli as served by Vercel. Third-party tags are excluded: they are served from someone else's egress and cost us nothing. Taken 2026-09-09 with playwright-core driving Chrome Beta 154 headless, a fresh browser context per run, waiting until the network went quiet. 976.1 KB on the recorded basis — document, script and images — stable to 0.0 KB across three runs at 2560x1209 and two at 1280x720. Split at first contentful paint the same load is 122.6-158.2 KB up to FCP and 1012.9 KB at settle across 80 requests, which is the finding that fixes what this number means: the basis is the SETTLE figure, and calling it 'first paint' was wrong about the instant, not about the bytes.
wireCalibration.measuredAgainst: the production deployment of v1.0.0-beta.230, measured 2026-10-07. playwright-core driving Chrome Beta headless, fresh context per run (cold HTTP cache), visibilityState 'visible', no scroll, settled to network idle plus five seconds, first-party (aglyn.com) encodedBodySize as served: 553.0 KB across 54 requests, within 0.1 KB across three runs at 2560x1209 and 535.7 KB at 1280x720. sourceGraphBytes is the published page's module graph at the v1.0.0-beta.230 tag, the source that deployment was built from. Third-party tags on the same load (connect.facebook.net 200.7 KB, Google and LinkedIn tags) are excluded as before. The previous 748.5 KB described v1.0.0-beta.104 against an 885376-byte graph; the graph grew 13.9% since, which this re-measure exists to catch, and the page that ships it is lighter on the wire, not heavier.
wireCalibration.notMeasured: /press is not a second reference. It is a brand-asset download page: forcing its 45 images plus its asset fetches pulled 17.7 MB, which is a download and not a page render, and no page-view rate should be calibrated against it.
wireCalibration.scrollBasis: This figure is SETTLE, not first paint. Lazy chunks below the fold are not in it, and neither is cross-route prefetch (see crossRoutePrefetch). Settle is the basis the rate is priced on: every visitor pays it, where a scroll is optional. Pricing on the 122.6-158.2 KB that reaches first contentful paint would price a fraction of the bytes the visit actually costs.
wireCalibration.crossRoutePrefetch: EXCLUDED, deliberately. A scrolled measurement of the same page read 1928.7 KB, of which about 919 KB was Next.js prefetching OTHER routes — /pricing at 54.9 KB, /legal/terms at 36.8 KB and so on — because the footer's links entered the viewport. Those routes bill as their own page views, so counting them here would charge for the same bytes twice. The 1338.9 KB 'scrolled' figure recorded previously most likely carries the same inflation, which is why it is not carried forward as an alternative basis.
wireCalibration.whyTheRateMoved: Re-pegged 2026-09-09 from a 627 KB basis to 1012.8 KB (AGL-2711), against a page then measuring 976.1 KB. Within the same day the AGL-2710 deferral work shipped and the page fell to 748.5 KB, so the basis now sits 35.3% above the measurement rather than the 3.8% it was set at. THE SURPLUS IS REVIEWED AND DELIBERATELY KEPT (owner, 2026-09-09): the standing reason for pegging high is that it is easy to charge less later and hard to charge more, and pricing twice in one day is the churn the measure-once-price-once rule exists to prevent. WHAT IT COSTS, so the next reader does not have to re-derive it: at 748.5 KB the true cost is $0.000119378 per view, so the billed rate is 1.76x true cost rather than the 1.30x the published 'at cost + 30%' claim states. That is the argument for lowering it, and the reason to revisit once the page has settled. Lowering is MARGIN-NEUTRAL: ESTIMATED_PAGE_TRANSFER_BYTES is the paired half, and moving both leaves one GB of included bandwidth at $0.16724, so no tier margin moves. A re-peg to a 748.5 KB basis would publish $0.1552 per 1,000. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-07 (AGL-3634): the basis now sits 83.1% above a 553.0 KB page, so the billed rate is 2.38x true cost rather than 1.76x. The rate is NOT moved by this record: a price change is the owner's decision, and lowering stays margin-neutral as described above (re-peg BOTH rate tables and ESTIMATED_PAGE_TRANSFER_BYTES together).
